questions.question: Studies show that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than when headlights are off.
Often confusing to other drivers.
Less safe than when headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than when headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. During the day, a motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure, you should:

options.text: Look at the tire to estimate pressure.
Use a tire gauge.
Squeeze the tire with your hand.
Compare the tire height to another tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a tire gauge.
questions.explanation: Always use a tire gauge to check pressure before every ride. A tire that is under-inflated may look fine, so looking at it is not enough.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride in:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
Any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A helmet that provides the best protection should:

options.text: Have a few cracks.
Not be certified.
Have frayed straps.
Fit snugly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a good choice for riding clothes?

options.text: A jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely
Boots or shoes that cover your ankles
Leather gloves
A baseball cap to cover your hair

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap to cover your hair
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not protect you and is not a substitute for a helmet.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection usually takes:

options.text: A few minutes and should be done no more than once a month.
A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
Over an hour and should be performed by a mechanic.
Over an hour and must only be done if you will carry a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: A few minutes and should be done before every ride.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough pre-ride inspection before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding, your ability to ride safely:

options.text: Means you cannot be arrested.
Means your skills will not be affected.
Does not eliminate all effects of alcohol.
Is fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not eliminate all effects of alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even if you consume only one drink per hour. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When braking, you should use:

options.text: Only the front brake.
Only the rear brake.
Both brakes.
Either brake, but never both at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes at the same time when stopping. The brakes work best when used together.

questions.question: What can you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Ride with your headlight on.
Swerve within your lane to draw attention.
Raise your arms.
Avoid using your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take evasive action if needed.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks consumed four hours ago means about four drinks remain in the system.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need to.
It limits how far you can see to the sides.
It is usually uncomfortable.
It has no markings or tags.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see as far to the sides as you need to.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels and markings that show the manufacturer's name, instructions, and the safety standards they meet.

questions.question: What fabric gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Wool
Polyester

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: For the best protection, riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather
Wool
Polyester
Silk

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another strong material to protect your hands.

questions.question: Where should you find the best information about your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual
A general book about motorcycles
Someone who rides a different type of motorcycle
A television show about motorcycle riding

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before you ride it for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual has information specific to your bike.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your ability to ride?

options.text: Yes, it can affect your judgment and riding ability.
No, there is usually no effect on the body.
It affects the body, but only for a short time.
It affects the body, but drinking coffee will stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can affect your judgment and riding ability.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding skills and judgment. Your body needs time to remove alcohol. Coffee will not speed this up.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of having an accident?

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic so other drivers don't notice you.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep safe distance from other vehicles and look ahead for hazards.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt fails, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: You have been drinking. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Side effects from drinking may still remain.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects from drinking may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your system. Your ability and judgment can still be impaired even if you wait.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.
Speed up to put more distance between you.
Come to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If you can, change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: Downshifting to a lower gear is also called:

options.text: Engine braking
Acceleration
Upshifting
Coasting

questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear works like using the brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for new riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It is encouraged to help riders practice different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle, which changes how it handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a bridge grating?

options.text: Always stay on the far right side of your lane.
Always stay on the far left side of your lane.
Slowly zigzag back and forth across the grating.
Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Bridge gratings may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Keep a steady speed and ride straight. Zigzagging to fight the weave is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride more slowly than usual.
Start slowing down later than usual.
Try to fit into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. It will speed up more slowly, turn more slowly, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, slow down sooner, leave more space between you and other vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What is the most important thing you can do to survive a crash?

options.text: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
Wear shorts.
Wear sneakers.
Wear goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a good helmet that is fastened securely.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that is fastened securely is the best way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist choose their lane position?

options.text: Pick one favorite spot in the lane and always stay there.
Weave back and forth constantly to keep other drivers away.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
Do not worry about lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
Your body removes the alcohol faster.
The effects of alcohol are less noticeable.
You are more likely to avoid being stopped by police.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, more alcohol builds up in your body. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Can common drugs like cold tablets affect riding ability?

options.text: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
No, they usually do not affect riding ability.
No, they pose no risk.
No, they are always safe because they are sold over-the-counter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they can affect your ability to ride safely.
questions.explanation: Almost all drugs, including over-the-counter medications, can affect your riding ability. Know the side effects of any drug before you ride.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Why are mirror checks important?

options.text: They are not important.
They should only be done on long trips.
They should be part of your regular scanning routine.
They are not helpful because you cannot do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should be part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular routine. Check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may cross into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
You will usually stay in your lane.
It is acceptable because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you enter a turn or curve.
